claims.text: Using density functional theory to model oxidation reactions can improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of metals or alloys.
Density functional theory can be applied to oxidation-reaction modeling.
Oxidation-reaction kinetics serve as the structural mediator between DFT modeling and oxidation resistance.
Ab initio calculations can provide an understanding of oxidation-reaction kinetics.
DFT oxidation modeling leads to improved oxidation resistance.
The proposed effect applies in a high-temperature regime.
Reduced oxidation rate and reduced material degradation would indicate improved oxidation resistance.

contradictions.description: The intervention defines DFT as a computational modeling activity, whereas the experiment treats 'DFT-modeled samples' and non-modeled samples as physically distinct treatment groups. No material-design or processing change derived from DFT is specified that could create those sample groups.
